correctness.rationale: Writing δ=x-y and k(u)=floor(squ), δ'= (1-2c)(sq δ - k(x)+k(y)). At neutral 1-2c=±1/q, hence qδ'≡±s qδ (mod 1), pointwise even at branch boundaries. Thus H=cos(2πqδ) and ρ=dist(δ,q^-1 Z) are exact first integrals, and |δ_t|>=ρ0. Its zero-level set is a finite union of lines, planar null, giving almost-everywhere nonapproach. For independent initial uniform coordinates, qX mod1,qY mod1 are independent Haar uniform; distance of their difference to integers is uniform [0,1/2], so ρ uniform [0,1/(2q)] and P(ever |δ|<eps)<=2qeps. Each ergodic invariant measure concentrates on one null level set and is singular. Any ACIP has atomless ρ marginal, whose invariant nontrivial level restrictions yield uncountably many ACIPs; no existence asserted. Exact rational q3,q4,q7 and both signs/couplings corroborate congruence.
